observation: Both pages center their content in a fixed-width column on a 1440px viewport. The original's white column is about 1080px wide (x≈180–1260) with dark side gutters. The AI-built page's container is about 1000–1040px wide (x≈220–1220) with wide side margins.

The original's body background is near-black rgb(17,17,17), with a subtle texture at the top that turns flat at about y=900. The AI-built page's body background is measured as off-white rgb(251,252,250), but judge G reported seeing a dark, textured charcoal ground.

The Mohawk text '-Wa'tkwanonhwerá:ton'' with a small cartoon or owl graphic appears on both pages. The original puts it in a small dark strip above the white column, at top-left. The AI-built page centers it under the hero as an owl GIF with empty alt text.
The original centers a large 660x145 GIF logo (green 'KANIEN'KÉHA' wordmark with tagline) in its header. The AI-built page puts a smaller 260x57 GIF wordmark on the left of a white header bar.

Each page has exactly one h1. The original's h1 is empty (the logo image stands in for it), styled at 36px, weight 900, in grey Open Sans. The AI-built page's h1 reads 'Kanienkeha.net' at 44.8px, weight 700, in deep green Helvetica Neue. Both are centered.

The original's primary nav is a textured green bar with 10 uppercase bold white items separated by thin dark dividers. The AI-built page's nav is a flat, full-width deep-green bar rgb(12,107,56) with a thin lighter-green bottom rule.
On both pages the nav items wrap onto a second row: 'CONTACT' on the original and 'Register' on the AI-built page.
The original marks the active HOME nav item with an orange-red fill and a dropdown chevron. The AI-built page has no such active-item highlight.
The original has a wide 'Search Dictionary' search bar under the nav, with a green frame and a square green arrow submit (forms: 2). The AI-built page has no search form.

Both pages offer the suggested searches apple, colors and numbers. The original shows them as a 'Try these:' line of comma-separated orange text links. The AI-built page shows them as white rounded chips, each with a 32px green square icon and a bold sans label, after a grey serif 'Try a sample search:' label.

The original ends a centered grey welcome paragraph with a bold red-orange text CTA, 'Support us on Patreon!'. The AI-built page has a centered hero with a filled green 'Support us on Patreon' button (6px radius, 11px 22px padding) and an outlined 'About the project' button.

The original's main body is a two-column layout: a ~583px left column for the map and word list, and a ~417px right sidebar of widgets, built with flex and floats (display_grid 0). The AI-built page stacks full-width content sections vertically (section 9, display_grid 8, display_flex 20) and uses two-column splits inside some sections.

The map illustration (map-nap.png, '200+ Locations' Kanienkeha Map) appears on both pages. The original puts it at the top of the left column, with a green 'MOST RECENT' title bar overlaying its bottom edge. The AI-built page gives it its own Map section as a linked 482px image on the right, with heading, text and button on the left and descriptive alt text.

The original lists recent dictionary entries as about 50 full-width rows separated by hairline rules: the English term as a green link on the left, the Mohawk translation in grey on the right. The AI-built page uses a 3-column grid of white link cards grouped under h3s (Phrases, Commands — daily routine, Occupations), each with a bold green serif Mohawk term above a grey English gloss.

In the original, each list entry is an article whose h2 is 16px bold, the same size as body text (51 articles, 58 h2s). In the AI-built page, entries are li anchors holding two spans (0 articles), and the h2s are section headings at 27.2px bold.
On both pages the Mohawk terms use orthography with diacritics (á, ò, ó), colon length marks and glottal-stop apostrophes.

Both pages show the long term 'Ohén:ton Í:rate ne Ionterihwaienstahkhwaniónhkhwa' (Education Director). On the original it overlaps the English link text with no wrapping. On the AI-built page it wraps to two lines and makes its card 104px tall instead of 75px.
The AI-built page lists gendered occupation pairs as separate cards with '(male)' or '(female)' in the gloss, for example Steelworker (male) and Steelworker (female).

Both pages paginate the entry list with numbered boxes and Next and Last links. The original uses square boxes: the current page in red-orange, the others in pale mint with white text. The AI-built page uses white rounded boxes on a full-width green strip whose labels judge G could not see.

Both palettes are built on greens. The original combines several greens (#12a465, #0ca25f, #48bd8a, mint #b7e2cf) with a red-orange accent #e74c3c (82 text elements) on black and white. The AI-built page is a monochrome green system: deep green rgb(12,107,56), brighter green rgb(18,151,79) and mint rgb(230,244,236) on mostly white cards, with no red-orange.
On the AI-built page, Occupation cards carry a pink/magenta left border while Phrases and Commands cards carry a green one, a category-coded accent.

The original's body text is grey #707b77 (300 elements) and #666, and it splits link colors by role: green for entries, red-orange for sidebar and footer links, orange for the suggestions. The AI-built page's body text is dark rgb(38,38,46), its links are mostly green rgb(12,107,56), and secondary lines use muted grey rgb(91,91,104).

The original sets body and list text in Verdana (668 elements) and headings in Open Sans (93), with FontAwesome for icons. The AI-built page sets body text, card titles and the blockquote in Georgia serif (291) and the h1, h2s, nav and buttons in Helvetica Neue/Arial (90).
The original's body text is 16px on a 24px line height (1.5), with smaller sidebar paragraphs. The AI-built page's body text is 17px on a 28.05px line height (about 1.65).

The original's section headings (#WORDOFTHEDAY, SPREAD THE WORD!, etc.) are bold grey uppercase, each with a small green line-art illustration at the left and a green underline rule. The AI-built page's h2s are sentence-case 27.2px bold sans. Some have an icon image inline or above, such as the 40px icon in 'Spread the word' and the turtle-like icon in 'Word of the day'.

An illustration of signs reading Resources, Blogging, Talk, Culture and Language accompanies the blog links on both pages. The original uses it as a banner heading the blog list in the sidebar. The AI-built page shows it as a 392x191 image (protest.png) on the right of the blog section, with alt text.

Both pages show blog links as a stacked list with thin separators. The original's are red-orange titles that wrap to two lines in the sidebar. The AI-built page's are bold green serif links in a 482px column, followed by a grey 'There is also a separate blog.' line.

Both pages offer English and Kanienkeha options with a UK flag and a red flag. The original shows them under a 'Choose your Language!' h3 in the sidebar with 32px flags. The AI-built page shows them as two outlined pill switchers with 20px flags on the right of the header.

The original's #WORDOFTHEDAY widget is mostly empty space with a loading spinner (iframes: 2). The AI-built page's Word of the day is a centered white rounded card with an icon, an h2, a one-line description with a bold hashtag, and an outlined 'Pull up a random word' button.

The original's social links are a strip of three square icon tiles (Facebook green, Twitter mint, Instagram blue) with no gaps, plus a 'MohDictionary' list of six links with 16px favicons all labeled 'mohdictionary'. The AI-built page uses one row of seven white pill buttons; only Newsletter and Gumroad carry small icons, and the rest are text only.

The original's sidebar stacks full-width flat rectangular buttons: a green 'Random Word' and a salmon-red 'Become a patron on Patreon.'. The AI-built page's buttons have a small radius (6px) and come in two styles: filled green with white bold sans text (Patreon, Open the map, Upload notes) and white with a green outline (About the project, Pull up a random word).
Neither page has button elements (buttons 0). Calls to action are styled anchors on both.

An upload-notes promo with a notebook illustration appears on both pages. The original has it as a sidebar widget: bold grey h3, small paragraph, and a 417px illustration (notes-4.jpg) with empty alt. The AI-built page gives it a full section: heading, text and a green button on the left, a 482px illustration (notes.jpg) with descriptive alt on the right.

Both pages show site statistics in which 'Categories' and 'Blog' are links. The original's 'TOTAL SITE NUMBERS' sidebar list pairs bold grey labels with square green number badges (2650, 159, 260, 10), and the linked labels are red. The AI-built page shows four equal white cards in a row, each with a large bold green number, and the linked labels are green sans.
The AI-built page puts a small progress-style image (forum-stats1.png) next to a muted line, 'Goal: roughly 10,000 words.'

Both pages include the founder's welcome. The original places it low in the sidebar under 'SHE:KON/GREETINGS:' as a long paragraph in small grey text, signed 'Nia:wen/Thank you Benjamin Doolittle'. The AI-built page places it near the top in a mint rounded card (about 16px radius) as a serif blockquote, with illustrations on the right.

Both pages pair Mohawk words with English glosses. The original joins them with a slash ('SHE:KON/GREETINGS:', 'Nia:wen/Thank you'). The AI-built page puts the Mohawk term in bold and the English in a small muted parenthetical, as in 'She:kon (hello)' and 'Nia:wen (thank you)'.
The AI-built page's founder card stacks three flat green illustrations (a hugging pair, a longhouse, a 'we are friends' strip) at their native sizes, with no shared alignment edge.
Both pages illustrate with flat green line-art or vector images. The original has 11 images, and the AI-built page has 18 in mixed GIF, PNG and JPG formats.

Both footers are green bands that credit Doolittle Productions. The original has an illustrated skyline of trees, figures and a longhouse above a flat green bar, with 'kanienkeha.net' at left and the credit at right. The AI-built page has a plain deep-green band with white underlined links (About, Contact, Sitemap, Donate) and a left-aligned credit line.

Below its green footer, on the black background, the original has a centered row of red-orange text links (Home, About, Donate, Resources, Sitemap, Register, Contact) and a 'Follow us on Twitter, Facebook & Facebook' line with icons.

Corner treatment differs. The original is almost entirely square: 764 elements with no radius, 16 at 1–7px, 2 at 8–15px, 1 at 16px or more, and 11 pills. The AI-built page uses more small rounding: 61 at 1–7px, 9 at 8–15px, 9 at 16px or more, and 0 pills.
The original uses some effects: 18 box-shadows, 7 gradients, 166 transitions, 8 animations and 15 transforms. The AI-built page has none of these. Neither page uses backdrop blur.

The original's DOM is heavy and div-based: 317 divs, 60 scripts, 24 stylesheets, 112 inline style attributes, and 416 unique classes across 1581 uses. The AI-built page is minimal: 26 divs, 0 scripts, 0 external stylesheets (one style block), 4 inline style attributes, and 27 unique classes across 153 uses. Neither uses utility-framework classes.

Both pages have main, footer and two nav landmarks. The original has 2 headers, 1 aside, 51 articles and no sections. The AI-built page has 1 header, 9 sections, 1 blockquote, and no aside or articles.
The AI-built page includes a skip-to-content link positioned off-screen at x=-999.

The original's heading hierarchy is flat: an empty h1, then 58 h2s mixing list entries and sidebar widgets, and 2 h3s. The AI-built page has an h1 'Kanienkeha.net', 8 section h2s, and 3 h3s under 'Most recent entries'.

The original's metadata is rich: Open Graph, Twitter card and Apple web-app meta tags, 3 JSON-LD blocks, lang en-GB, and an all-caps title 'KANIEN'KÉHA LANGUAGE INITIATIVE (Mohawk Dictionary) • …'. The AI-built page has only charset, viewport and description meta, no JSON-LD, lang en, and the title 'Kanienkeha.net — An Open Source Endangered Language Initiative'.

Both pages use bilingual English/Mohawk copy with no emoji. The original uses short exclamatory CTAs (4 exclamation marks, 0 em dashes, 440 words). The AI-built page uses plain English sentences (0 exclamation marks, 2 em dashes, 492 words).
The original is 3590px tall, and its sidebar ends before the word list, leaving empty white space beside the list's end. The AI-built page is 5654px tall, a stack of full-width sections.
The AI-built page separates sections with thin light hairlines across the viewport, with about 50px of vertical padding per section.
Judge G saw dark paragraph text rendered on a dark ground, so the hero paragraph, the h3 labels, and the Map and Upload paragraphs were nearly invisible and left blank gaps above buttons.

Alt text handling differs. The original has 2 images with no alt attribute, and several social favicons carry a wrong alt (a Facebook URL). The AI-built page has 0 missing alts: decorative images get empty alt, and content images (logo, map, protest, notes) get descriptive alt.
